{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table delivered a large, clear fish outline, with a rounded body, a swooshy tail and a nose, and nearly every standing domino was connected to the start for the push. I contributed to that by finding and fixing the break just before the nose, which had left the nose stretch disconnected from the start. I also closed a stray domino in the belly seam later on.

Execution: I spent my time on careful inspection of the run, checking it repeatedly from the start through the top line, nose, belly and tail to see what would actually fall. I restacked the three dominoes that needed standing back up, each at a spot where the fall had stalled. I also flagged an overlap at the belly ends so the bottom line would leave from a true end.

Collaboration: I kept hands off areas where teammates were working so we avoided bumping each other, and I told people before I touched a spot. I suggested splitting the long bottom line so Priya could carry the tail end back toward the belly while Maya worked on from the nose. That kept the work moving in the last five minutes. I also confirmed to the table when the nose was fixed so Tom could carry on.

Leadership: I helped set the sequence for the second half of the build: who carries which stretch, where they meet, and when everyone steps back. I called for hands off before the push so nothing got knocked at the last moment. I backed Priya's fish concept at the outset and kept the group focused on getting one connected run.

Overall, I think my inspection and the fixes at the nose and belly were central to getting the whole run to fall as one piece, though the fish itself was a team effort.", "my_share_percent": 30}
